_**Om Shanti Om**_ (transl. and released internationally as _**Peace Be With You**_[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-6)) is a 2007 Indian [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi")-language [masala film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_film "Masala film") written and directed by [Farah Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farah_Khan "Farah Khan"), co-written by [Mayur Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayur_Puri "Mayur Puri") and [Mushtaq Shiekh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushtaq_Shiekh "Mushtaq Shiekh"), and produced by [Gauri Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauri_Khan "Gauri Khan") under [Red Chillies Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment"). The film stars [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan"), [Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone") (in her [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") film debut), [Arjun Rampal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun_Rampal "Arjun Rampal"), [Shreyas Talpade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreyas_Talpade "Shreyas Talpade"), [Kirron Kher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirron_Kher "Kirron Kher"). Spanning four odd decades, the narrative follows Om Prakash Makhija, an obscure 1970s actor in love with female superstar Shanti, who dies in a suspicious on-set fire that kills Shanti and is reincarnated 30 years later as the superstar Om Kapoor, determined to punish the person who ignited the blaze with the help of Shanti's lookalike.

Farah Khan began development for the film while directing the musical _[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ (2002), and it began production after its leads were cast. The film's title is borrowed from a song from [Subhash Ghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhash_Ghai "Subhash Ghai")'s thriller _[Karz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karz\_(film) "Karz (film)")_ (1980), which also features in the opening credits. _Om Shanti Om_'s soundtrack was composed by [Vishal–Shekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal%E2%80%93Shekhar "Vishal–Shekhar"), with the lyrics written by [Javed Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar "Javed Akhtar"), Vishal Dadlani, and [Kumaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaar "Kumaar"). The background score was composed by [Sandeep Chowta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandeep_Chowta "Sandeep Chowta"). The film is notable for its cameo appearances from [Indian film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_film "Indian film") celebrities.

Produced on a budget of ₹40 [crore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crore "Crore") (US$9.67 million), _Om Shanti Om_ emerged as the [highest grossing Hindi film of 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Hindi_films_of_2007 "List of Hindi films of 2007") and the then-highest grossing Hindi film of all time. The soundtrack was also critical and commercial success, becoming the highest-selling [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album") of the year in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). The film received positive reviews from critics, with praise for its story, direction, cast performances, production design, and soundtrack. _Om Shanti Om_ received a leading 13 nominations at the [53rd Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/53rd_Filmfare_Awards "53rd Filmfare Awards"), winning for [Best Female Debut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Female_Debut "Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut") (Padukone) and [Best Special Effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Special_Effects "Filmfare Award for Best Special Effects").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-7)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In 1977, Om Prakash "Omi" Makhija, a [junior artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_artist "Junior artist") in Mumbai, dreams of becoming a renowned actor. He lives with his widowed mother, Bela, and his friend Pappu Master in a small [chawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chawl "Chawl"). Omi adores the glamorous superstar actress Shantipriya, often expressing his feelings in front of her film poster. One night, he and Pappu sneak into the premiere of Shanti's film, _Dreamy Girl_, in disguise, making a memorable impression on her. Later, Omi, inebriated, gives a heartfelt acceptance speech to Pappu and local children, pretending to have won an award.

Omi and Pappu land minor roles at R.C. Studios, owned by the egotistical producer Mukesh Mehra, who also launched Shanti's career. During a shoot, Shanti gets trapped in a fire but is rescued by Omi. The two become friends, and although Omi initially lies about being a [Tamil film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_cinema "Tamil cinema") star to impress her, he eventually confesses the truth. Shanti grows close to Omi, and with Pappu's help, they share a memorable evening date together at the studio.

Omi overhears a heated argument between Shanti and Mukesh, revealing that they are secretly married. Shanti is furious when she learns that Mukesh plans to marry the daughter of the distributor for his upcoming film, _Om Shanti Om_. She reveals to Mukesh that she is pregnant with his child, which seems to please him. Heartbroken, Omi avoids Shanti.

One night, Mukesh takes Shanti to the future set of _Om Shanti Om_, claiming he will cancel the film and have a grand wedding there to make their marriage public. Omi visits Shanti but is devastated to see her with Mukesh; he leaves without either noticing. However, once Omi leaves, Mukesh reveals his true colours to Shanti, confessing that his actual plan is to kill her and their unborn child to avoid any impedance in his career as a producer. He lights up the set on fire and locks Shanti inside. Despite his attempts to rescue her after Mukesh leaves, Omi gets beaten by Mukesh's guards and is thrown out by an explosion by the time he can get to Shanti. The set burns down with Shanti inside. Omi is later struck by the car of actor Rajesh Kapoor, whose wife Lovely is in labor. Rajesh brings Omi to the hospital, but he dies from his injuries, while Rajesh and Lovely welcome a baby boy named Om Kapoor.

30 years later, Om Kapoor aka O. K., now a successful yet arrogant actor, suffers from [pyrophobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrophobia "Pyrophobia") and frequently encounters Bela, who believes him to be her son. He dismisses her as delusional, and Pappu, now old, tries to explain the truth, but Bela remains unconvinced.

While shooting at the abandoned R.C. Studios, O.K. experiences vivid flashbacks of Omi trying to rescue Shanti and later unwittingly delivers Omi's old drunken speech at a [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") event. Pappu watches him on TV and realizes that Omi has reincarnated as Om Kapoor. At a party celebrating his victory, O.K. meets Mukesh, now known as Mike, who proposes a film collaboration; an introduction to him causes O.K. to fully remember his previous life. Om finally reunites with Bela and Pappu at the old chawl, and together with Om's assistant Anwar, they plan to expose Mukesh's crimes.

O.K. resumes filming _Om Shanti Om_ at the old studio after convincing Mukesh to revive the project, and after many failed auditions of other actresses, hires Sandhya "Sandy" Bansal, an aspiring actress who is an exact doppelgänger of Shanti and a huge fangirl of Om. Pappu and Bela start training her to behave exactly like Shanti. Om initially hides his plan but later reveals the truth to Sandy, who promises to help him. At the film's inauguration, Bela, disguised as a witch, and Sandy, disguised as Shanti's ghost, try to scare Mukesh into confessing. Despite a fake inauguration plan gone wrong, a photograph of Shanti inexplicably catches fire, unsettling Mukesh and confusing Om and Pappu.

During a masquerade ball for the film's music launch, Om indirectly hints at Mukesh's guilt through Shanti's story. However, Sandy accidentally reveals her ruse by injuring herself, proving she is not a ghost. Mukesh, suspicious of the film reels, chases Sandy but is knocked out by a chandelier. When he regains consciousness, O.K. confronts him in the empty venue about Shanti's murder. Mukesh mocks O.K., claiming there is no proof and revealing he knows Sandy is not Shanti. Sandy then appears, disclosing that Mukesh had buried Shanti alive under the chandelier after discovering she had survived the initial fire. She even foretells that Shanti's body will be found, which will be proof of murder for the court. Both Om and Mukesh are perturbed at how deeply she knows Shanti's tragic story; in the confrontation that follows, Om finally overcomes his pyrophobia and defeats Mukesh, who is crushed to death by the falling chandelier.

Pappu and Anwar arrive with the real Sandy. Om then realizes that the woman with him is actually Shanti's ghost, who was also responsible for the unexplained aids in his plan. With her death now avenged, Om and Shanti bid each other a tearful goodbye, and he reunites with Sandy while Shanti runs up the stairs and disappears, having attained peace.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Development")]

In 2002, [Farah Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farah_Khan "Farah Khan") worked as a choreographer for the musical _[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ in London, which she felt presented a "clichéd and outdated version" of the Indian film industry.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) She thought that the musical would not be successful if released in India.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) She instead thought of a new story, writing her initial thoughts about the subject on [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber")'s letterhead while staying in his house.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-9) Later in 2006, Farah began to work on her next project, which was tentatively titled _Happy New Year_. Amid speculations that [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") would star in _Happy New Year_, the actor rejected the first draft of the film, upon which Farah's husband and editor [Shirish Kunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirish_Kunder "Shirish Kunder") reminded her of the story she had conceived while in London.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10)_Happy New Year_, which was to mark [Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone")'s Hindi debut, was put on hiatus and revived more than 8 years later under the [same title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_New_Year_(2014_film) "Happy New Year (2014 film)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-11)

Farah completed writing the first script of _Om Shanti Om_ within two weeks.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-12) She set the first half in the 1970s as she felt the [Hindi films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") made during that period were much more influential than those made in other periods, particularly the 1980s, which she felt was a period when "the worst movies were made". She also included many references to the 1970s, which were also prevalent in films of that time. She said, "Everything in the first half is about the 70s—such as the mother who overacts, mouthing clichéd dialogues. Then there are cabarets, badminton and other stuff popular during that era."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) Shah Rukh's costumes were designed by [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar"), while [Manish Malhotra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manish_Malhotra "Manish Malhotra") designed Padukone's costumes. The rest of the cast had their costumes designed by Sanjeev Mulchandani.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-13)

In addition to directing the film, Farah co-wrote the story with [Mayur Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayur_Puri "Mayur Puri") and [Mushtaq Shiekh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushtaq_Shiekh "Mushtaq Shiekh"). She was also the film's choreographer. Puri wrote the screenplay and dialogues.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14) He completed the writing process in two months and rewrote the film's second half.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-15) Puri created the screenplay by writing his natural reaction to the characters as scenarios. He knew that despite being part of a crowd, junior artists do not want to be recognised as such, ruins their chances of landing a leading role in future. This was used in a sequence involving Shah Rukh and Talpade, who play junior artists. Puri blended different genres together in _Om Shanti Om_, which he felt was challenging. He used his personal memories from childhood for creating the 1970s.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-comic-16) Shirish Kunder was the editor, while V. Manikandan was the cinematographer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14)

[Sabu Cyril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabu_Cyril "Sabu Cyril") was the film's [production designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_designer "Production designer"). Sabu was first offered the [Mani Ratnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mani_Ratnam "Mani Ratnam")-directed _[Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru\_(2007\_film) "Guru (2007 film)")_ (2007) at a time when _Om Shanti Om_ was being planned, but ultimately chosen the latter due to his earlier commitment to Farah for her future project.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-17) Farah used two particular dialogues in the film: "When you want something badly, the whole universe conspires to give to you" and "In the end everything will be ok and if its not ok its not the end". These were used as Khan felt that it reflected her philosophy in her life.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-18) Farah stated that the film's opening scene was her most favourite in it.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-19) In 2008, Puri felt his most favourite dialogue from the ones he wrote would be the Filmfare Awards speech.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-comic-16) The film's title derives from the eponymous song from the film _[Karz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karz\_(film) "Karz (film)")_ (1980).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-20)[Om](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om "Om") is a Hindu mantra; _Om Shanti Om_ roughly translates to "Peace Be With You".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-22)

The film opens with the grandeur shot of the most famous songs of _Karz_ that is _Om Shanti Om_ featuring [Rishi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rishi_Kapoor "Rishi Kapoor") and [SRK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRK "SRK") as a junior film artist standing in the crowd.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-23)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Casting")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Deepika_Padukone_promoting_RACE_2_on_NACH_BALIYE_5.jpg/250px-Deepika_Padukone_promoting_RACE_2_on_NACH_BALIYE_5.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Deepika_Padukone_promoting_RACE_2_on_NACH_BALIYE_5.jpg)

[Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone") plays the love interest of Shah Rukh Khan's character in her Hindi film debut.

Shah Rukh was cast as the lead; he worked hard on his physique for a song sequence.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-24) He felt _Om Shanti Om_ was a "happy film".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-25)

Farah was advised by [Malaika Arora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaika_Arora "Malaika Arora") to cast Padukone as the female lead, who was suggested by [Wendell Rodricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendell_Rodricks "Wendell Rodricks"), under whom Padukone was working.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-26) She was cast without a screen test.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-27) Khan felt that she was "a beautiful, classic Indian beauty" who fit the role of an actor of the 1970s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) She was excited at the prospect of working with Shah Rukh and said, "I've grown up watching [Shah Rukh] and always admired him so much. To get to work with him... is quite wonderful. It was also fantastic that Farah showed faith in my talent and cast me opposite him."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-28)

In preparation for her role, Padukone watched several films of actresses [Helen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_(actress) "Helen (actress)") and [Hema Malini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") to study their body language.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-29) Her character was modelled after Malini and nicknamed Dreamy Girl after her the latter's nickname as Dream Girl.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-30) Rampal was approached by both Khan and Shah Rukh at the latter's New Year's Eve party. Rampal was initially reluctant to do the role as he felt it was "too evil" for someone like him. With persuasion from Shah Rukh, he agreed. Rampal wore a mustache in the film which was suggested by Shah Rukh.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10) Shreyas Talpade played a supporting role as the best friend of Khan's character. After the release of _Iqbal_ (2005) and completing the filming of _Dor_, Talpade, who attended the same gym as Khan, was called for a narration of what would be _Om Shanti Om_. He agreed to do the role.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-late-31)

[Kirron Kher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirron_Kher "Kirron Kher"), [Bindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bindu_(actress) "Bindu (actress)") and [Javed Sheikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Sheikh "Javed Sheikh") also appear in the film.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BOI_OSO_Cast-32) A further red carpet scene featuring a number of actors making guest appearances, including [R. Madhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._Madhavan "R. Madhavan") and [Farhan Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar") as well as [Prem Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Chopra "Prem Chopra"), [Shakti Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Kapoor "Shakti Kapoor") and [Vidhu Vinod Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidhu_Vinod_Chopra "Vidhu Vinod Chopra") was deleted from the film.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-33)

### Principal photography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Principal photography")]

_Om Shanti Om_ was made on a budget of ₹40 crore.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BOI-2) The first scene to be filmed was one where Talpade's character tells Shah Rukh's character that he will be a hero; Shah Rukh was an hour late for filming.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-late-31) Farah was pregnant with triplets while filming and experienced difficulties while shooting, she would constantly vomit while directing the film.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-34) The film was shot entirely in sync sound; Farah dismissed rumours of Padukone's voice being dubbed.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-35) In 2015, however, [Mona Ghosh Shetty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mona_Ghosh_Shetty "Mona Ghosh Shetty") admitted to have dubbed for Padukone in the film.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-36) The fake fight scene involving a stuffed tiger was inspired by a similar scene in the film _Tarzan 303_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10) Old cars owned by actors [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") and [Hema Malini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") were used for filming for authenticity.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-mtv-37)

A number of references to real life was also filmed, including a scene in which Om rescues Shanti from a fire, which was a spoof of [Sunil Dutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Dutt "Sunil Dutt") rescuing [Nargis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nargis "Nargis") from a fire on the sets of _[Mother India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother\_India "Mother India")_ (1957). For a shot involving a Filmfare Awards ceremony, Khan stood on the red carpet of an actual Filmfare Award ceremony and requested actors to dictate dialogues as she stated. The song "Dhoom Taana" has digitally altered guest appearances, which included [Sunil Dutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Dutt "Sunil Dutt") from _[Amrapali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrapali\_(film) "Amrapali (film)")_ (1966), [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") from _[Sachaa Jhutha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachaa\_Jhutha "Sachaa Jhutha")_ (1970) and [Jeetendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeetendra "Jeetendra") from _[Jay Vejay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay\_Vejay "Jay Vejay")_ (1977).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-38) Farah wanted to film [Shakira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakira "Shakira") for filming a special appearance had made her commit a few days for the role. Due to the uncertainty of her dates, the idea was scrapped.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-mtv-37)

In February 2007, a filming schedule was completed in Film City. It was then reported that filming would move outdoors after Shah Rukh completed filming for _[Kaun Banega Crorepati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaun\_Banega\_Crorepati "Kaun Banega Crorepati")_.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-39) The visuals of the song "Deewangi Deewangi" where Om meets Mukesh, was heavily inspired by a scene featuring [Jeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeet_(actor) "Jeet (actor)") and [Priyanshu Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priyanshu_Chatterjee "Priyanshu Chatterjee") from [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language") film _Bidhatar Lekha_, which was also based on the theme of reincarnation and coincidentally was released in April 2007.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-40) It was shot over a period of six days.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10) In October 2007, [Abhishek Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhishek_Bachchan "Abhishek Bachchan") finished filming for his cameo appearance; he shot between 10 and 2 in the night for his screen time of about one and a half minutes.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-41) Filming of the last sequence and the end-credit song was done in [Film City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_City,_Mumbai "Film City, Mumbai").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-42) Farah continued the tradition of featuring an end-credits song beginning with _[Main Hoon Na](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main\_Hoon\_Na "Main Hoon Na")_ (2004).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-43)

_Om Shanti Om_ was produced by Shah Rukh's wife [Gauri Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauri_Khan "Gauri Khan") under their [Red Chillies Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment") banner. While Marching Ants handled the publicity design, Gauri was the presenter. Shyam Kaushal, Amar Shetty and Shah Rukh were the action directors.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14) The film's final reel length was 4013.94 ft (1223.45 m).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14)

The [film score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_score "Film score") was composed by [Sandeep Chowta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandeep_Chowta "Sandeep Chowta") while the original songs featured in _Om Shanti Om_ were composed by the duo [Vishal–Shekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal%E2%80%93Shekhar "Vishal–Shekhar") with lyrics by [Javed Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar "Javed Akhtar"), [Kumaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaar "Kumaar") and Vishal Dadlani. One song was composed by Pyarelal of the [Laxmikant-Pyarelal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmikant-Pyarelal "Laxmikant-Pyarelal") duo.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-pyare-44) The vocals are provided by [KK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_(singer) "KK (singer)"), [Sukhwinder Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sukhwinder_Singh "Sukhwinder Singh"), Marianne, Nisha, [Caralisa Monteiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caralisa_Monteiro "Caralisa Monteiro"), [Shaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaan_(singer) "Shaan (singer)"), [Udit Narayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udit_Narayan "Udit Narayan"), [Shreya Ghoshal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreya_Ghoshal "Shreya Ghoshal"), [Sunidhi Chauhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunidhi_Chauhan "Sunidhi Chauhan"), Rahul Saxena, [Sonu Nigam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonu_Nigam "Sonu Nigam"), [Rahat Fateh Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahat_Fateh_Ali_Khan "Rahat Fateh Ali Khan"), [Richa Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richa_Sharma_(singer) "Richa Sharma (singer)"), [Abhijeet Bhattacharya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhijeet_Bhattacharya "Abhijeet Bhattacharya"), [DJ Aqeel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Aqeel "DJ Aqeel"), DJ G, Kiran Karnath, Jackie V, [Nikhil Chinapa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikhil_Chinapa "Nikhil Chinapa"), DJ Nawed and Zoheb.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-itunes-45) Trade reports predicted the album to be commercially successful even before its release.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-46) The soundtrack album of _Om Shanti Om_ was released on 18 September 2007 on CD,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-47) and was the highest-selling music album of the year in India, with sales of around 2 million units.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-itunes2-48)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-49)

#### Screening and statics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Screening and statics")]

_Om Shanti Om_ created a record of sorts by going in for an unheard of 2000 prints (worldwide) release. This was the highest number of prints (including digital) for any Indian movie at the time of its release.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-AGNIBAAN-50)

#### Pre-sale records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Pre-sale records")]

_Om Shanti Om_ set another record for registered pre-advance booking of 18,000 tickets in a chain of theatres in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") a few days before the advance booking was to start.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-Record_Pre_Advance_Booking-51) A special screening was conducted for Bollywood actors.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-sify.com-52)[Red Chillies Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment") had reportedly sold the world rights for the film to [Eros International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eros_Labs "Eros Labs") for an amount between Rs. 720–750 million. Baba Films, a production and distribution company, had offered a record Rs. 110 million for the rights to the Mumbai Circuit, surpassing the highest amount ever paid for the territory. As a marketing strategy, Amul advertised Shah Rukh.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-53)

### Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Home media")]

In the United Kingdom, the film was watched by 750,000 viewers on [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4") in 2010. This made it the year's most-watched foreign-language film on UK television, above the Japanese animated film _[Spirited Away](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirited\_Away "Spirited Away")_ and German animated film _[The Little Polar Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Little\_Polar\_Bear "The Little Polar Bear")_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-:22-54)

## Controversies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Controversies")]

### Spoof on Manoj Kumar

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Spoof on Manoj Kumar")]

[Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar") planned to sue the makers of _Om Shanti Om_ for showing his [body double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_double "Body double") in [bad taste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taste_(sociology)#Bad_taste "Taste (sociology)").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-cnnmanoj-55) Kumar added, "Are the Mumbai police so stupid that they can't recognise Manoj Kumar and lathicharge him in the '70s when he was a star?".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-toimanoj-56) Later, in a press conference, Shahrukh Khan and director Farah Khan accepted their mistake and apologised for the matter.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-toiapologise-57) Farah Khan even offered to cut the scene which Manoj Kumar felt was hurtful, but Kumar refused on grounds that, as Farah had stated, "I [Farah Khan] am like his daughter. He said, 'Betiyaan maafi nahi maangti' (Daughters don't ask for forgiveness). I told him that he could've called me and scolded me."[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-toiapologise-57) Later, Kumar said that though this incident was hurtful to him, he wishes to forgive, ignore, and move on, saying that he prefers to "see [Ram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama "Rama") in everyone and ignore the [Ravana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravana "Ravana")."[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-58)

Before the film's television premiere on Sony TV, Manoj Kumar filed for a stay on the television release, at civil court in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). On 8 August 2008, he won permanent injunction on the scenes in _Om Shanti Om_ that lampooned him. The court ordered the producers and [Sony Entertainment Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Entertainment_Television_(India) "Sony Entertainment Television (India)"), to edit the Manoj Kumar look-alike scenes before showing the film on the channel on 10 August 2008. It also ordered that the film could not be shown in any media—TV, DVD or Internet—without the scene being deleted.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-59)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-60)

### Plagiarism allegations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Plagiarism allegations")]

On 7 August 2008, before its television release, scriptwriter [Ajay Monga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajay_Monga "Ajay Monga") moved the Bombay High Court alleging that the basic storyline of the film was lifted from a film script he had emailed to Shah Rukh Khan in 2006. According to the petition, "Monga, along with one more writer [Hemant Hegde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemant_Hegde?action=edit&redlink=1 "Hemant Hegde (page does not exist)"), had registered the script with the Cine Writers Association (CWA) in September 2005. In January 2008, Cine Writers Association (CWA) rejected Monga's appeal at a special Executive Committee meeting. Thereafter, he approached the court to stay the film's screening on television. Though, on 6 August the court rejected Monga's plea for seeking a stay on the television telecast, it directed all the respondents including [Shahrukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan"), [Farah Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farah_Khan "Farah Khan"), [Red Chillies Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment"), [Gauri Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauri_Khan "Gauri Khan") (director Red Chillies) and film's co-writer Mushtaq Sheikh, to file their say by the next hearing on 29 September 2008.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-mir-61)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-62) In November 2008, the Film Writers' association sent a communication to Red Chillies and Ajay Monga that it had found similarities in _Om Shanti Om_ and Monga's script. The similarities were more than mere coincidences according to Sooni Taraporewala who chaired a special committee that has investigated the case on behalf of the Film Writers' association.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-63) The suit was dismissed in 2013 due to insufficient evidence.

Another allegation of [plagiarism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plagiarism "Plagiarism") came from [Rinki Bhattacharya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rinki_Bhattacharya "Rinki Bhattacharya"), daughter of late [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy"), who directed _[Madhumati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhumati "Madhumati")_ (1958). She threatened legal action against Red Chillies Entertainment and the producer-director of _Om Shanti Om_, as she felt that the film's second half was similar to _Madhumati_, also a rebirth saga.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-mir-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hum-64)

It has also been noted that the spoof trailer scene featuring Akshay Kumar is entirely copied from the Swedish film [Kopps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kopps "Kopps"), directed in 2003 by [Josef Fares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_Fares "Josef Fares").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-65)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-66)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Box office")]

_Om Shanti Om_ opened across 1100 cinemas in 3000 prints worldwide.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-67) The film's net gross (after deducting [entertainment tax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_tax "Entertainment tax")) was ₹794 million (US$19.2 million) in India.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-68) The film collected $2.62 million in the United Kingdom, $3.6 million in North America,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-69) and $3.93 million collectively from the rest of the world, which resulted in total overseas collections of $10,150,000,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BOI-2)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-:0-70) the fourth largest of all time as of 2010.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-:0-70) As a result of these collections, a worldwide gross of ₹150 crore (US$36.28 million) was accumulated.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-71)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Critical response")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 79% of 19 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.21/10.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-Rotten_Tomatoes-72)

#### India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: India")]

_Om Shanti Om_ was received positively by Indian film critics.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-73)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-IANS-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-75)[Taran Adarsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taran_Adarsh "Taran Adarsh") of _[Bollywood Hungama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood\_Hungama "Bollywood Hungama")_ gave it four stars out of five and writes, "_Om Shanti Om_ is Bollywood masala in its truest form and also, at its best" but notes, "the second half could've been crisper".[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-76)[Khalid Mohamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalid_Mohamed "Khalid Mohamed") of _[Hindustan Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan\_Times "Hindustan Times")_ gave the film four stars out of five and appreciated the performances, observing how Rampal is "consistently first-rate as the suave villain" while Padukone is "fantastic, so surprisingly assured that you marvel at her poised debut". He notes that "the enterprise belongs to Shah Rukh Khan, who tackles comedy, high drama and action with his signature style—spontaneous and intuitively intelligent. Six-pack or no-packs, he's the entertainer of the year in this valentine to the movies."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-77)

[Nikhat Kazmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikhat_Kazmi "Nikhat Kazmi") of _[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_ gave the film three and a half stars out of five and writes, "Farah Khan's re-birth saga literally makes an art of retro and paints the seventies pop culture in [Andy Warholish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Warhol "Andy Warhol") strokes". She called it an "unabashed tribute" to _Karz_.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-78)[Raja Sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Sen "Raja Sen") of _Rediff.com_ gave it three and a half stars out of five and applauded the performances of Shah Rukh, Padukone and Talpade. He writes, "_Om Shanti Om_ is an exultant, heady, joyous film reveling in Bollywood, and as at most parties where the bubbly flows free, there is much silly giggling and tremendous immaturity." He criticised the dialogues and excessive cameos in the film.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-79)

[Rajeev Masand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajeev_Masand "Rajeev Masand") of _[News18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News18 "News18")_ gave the film three stars out of five and writes, "Unpretentious and completely transparent in its intentions, _Om Shanti Om_ is an entertainer in the true sense of the word, mixing up genre elements like comedy, drama, action and emotion to create a heady broth of [Manmohan Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manmohan_Desai "Manmohan Desai")-style exaggerated entertainment." He compliments the dialogues "which so cleverly incorporates Bollywood's oldest clichés into these characters' everyday parlance."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-80) A commentator for _[Indo-Asian News Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Asian\_News\_Service "Indo-Asian News Service")_ felt that Shah Rukh's acting was repetitive and writes, "He needs to curtail his unwarranted superstar mannerisms even in a total masala film like _Om Shanti Om_", while complimenting the performances of Padukone, Rampal and Talpade.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-IANS-74)

Sudish Kamnath of _[The Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hindu "The Hindu")_ stated that the film is "an unabashed celebration of willing suspension of disbelief, calling it a "light-hearted tribute to Hindi cinema the way we know it and love it". He praised the performances of Shah Rukh, Padukone and Talpade, while criticising Rampal and Kher. He also praised the various spoofs, especially the ones directed at Manoj Kumar, [Sanjay Leela Bhansali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Leela_Bhansali "Sanjay Leela Bhansali") and Abhishek Bachchan.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-81) Writing for SantaBanta.com, Subhash K. Jha gave it one star out of five and criticised the spoofs "which keeps swinging from homage to imitation with infuriating artifice", writing, "The mood is one of patronizing and condescension rather than genuine admiration for an era that's gone with the wind".[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-82)

#### International

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: International")]

Tajpal Rathore of _[BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")_ gave it 4 out of 5 stars as well and stated, "Both a homage to and parody of Hindi Films, this cinematic feast delivered straight from the heart of the film industry will have you glued to your seats till the end."[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-83) Mark Medley of _[National Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Post "National Post")_ gave 3 stars and stated, "The film is a mess for all the right reasons; elements of comedy, drama, romance, action and the supernatural are packed in. But really, the plot is just a vehicle to get from one song-and-dance number to the next."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-84)_[AOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AOL "AOL")_ gave the film 3 out of 5 stars stating, "The movie consists of all the elements that are essentially called the 'navratnas' of Indian cinema– from joy to grief to romance to revenge. And she mixes these well to cook up a potboiler, which is sure to be a runaway hit."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-85)

## Legacy and Impact

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Legacy and Impact")]

[Nina Davuluri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nina_Davuluri "Nina Davuluri")'s talent for [Miss America 2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_America_2014 "Miss America 2014") was a Hindi film fusion dance choreographed by [Nakul Dev Mahajan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakul_Dev_Mahajan "Nakul Dev Mahajan") and performed to _Dhoom Taana_. It was the first time Indian film ever appeared on the [Miss America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_America "Miss America") stage and Davuluri is the first [Indian American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_American "Indian American") to win the competition.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-reut0916-108)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-insideedition-109)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-fusion-110)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-indiawest-111)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-TOA-112)

In Japan in 2017, _Om Shanti Om_ was remade into a musical, performed by the all-female troupe [Takarazuka Revue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takarazuka_Revue "Takarazuka Revue"), titled _Oomu Shanti Oumu_.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-113)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-114)

A book, titled _The Making of Om Shanti Om_ written by Mushtaq Sheikh, was released after the release of the film. The book gives an insight into the production and happenings behind the camera of the film.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-115)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-116)

_**Om Shanti Om**_ (transl. and released internationally as _**Peace Be With You**_[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-6)) is a 2007 Indian [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi")-language [masala film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_film "Masala film") written and directed by [Farah Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farah_Khan "Farah Khan"), co-written by [Mayur Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayur_Puri "Mayur Puri") and [Mushtaq Shiekh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushtaq_Shiekh "Mushtaq Shiekh"), and produced by [Gauri Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauri_Khan "Gauri Khan") under [Red Chillies Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment"). The film stars [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan"), [Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone") (in her [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") film debut), [Arjun Rampal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun_Rampal "Arjun Rampal"), [Shreyas Talpade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreyas_Talpade "Shreyas Talpade"), [Kirron Kher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirron_Kher "Kirron Kher"). Spanning four odd decades, the narrative follows Om Prakash Makhija, an obscure 1970s actor in love with female superstar Shanti, who dies in a suspicious on-set fire that kills Shanti and is reincarnated 30 years later as the superstar Om Kapoor, determined to punish the person who ignited the blaze with the help of Shanti's lookalike.

Farah Khan began development for the film while directing the musical _[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ (2002), and it began production after its leads were cast. The film's title is borrowed from a song from [Subhash Ghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhash_Ghai "Subhash Ghai")'s thriller _[Karz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karz\_(film) "Karz (film)")_ (1980), which also features in the opening credits. _Om Shanti Om_'s soundtrack was composed by [Vishal–Shekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal%E2%80%93Shekhar "Vishal–Shekhar"), with the lyrics written by [Javed Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Akhtar "Javed Akhtar"), Vishal Dadlani, and [Kumaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaar "Kumaar"). The background score was composed by [Sandeep Chowta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandeep_Chowta "Sandeep Chowta"). The film is notable for its cameo appearances from [Indian film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_film "Indian film") celebrities.

Produced on a budget of ₹40 [crore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crore "Crore") (US$9.67 million), _Om Shanti Om_ emerged as the [highest grossing Hindi film of 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Hindi_films_of_2007 "List of Hindi films of 2007") and the then-highest grossing Hindi film of all time. The soundtrack was also critical and commercial success, becoming the highest-selling [album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album "Album") of the year in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"). The film received positive reviews from critics, with praise for its story, direction, cast performances, production design, and soundtrack. _Om Shanti Om_ received a leading 13 nominations at the [53rd Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/53rd_Filmfare_Awards "53rd Filmfare Awards"), winning for [Best Female Debut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Female_Debut "Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut") (Padukone) and [Best Special Effects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Special_Effects "Filmfare Award for Best Special Effects").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-7)

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In 1977, Om Prakash "Omi" Makhija, a [junior artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_artist "Junior artist") in Mumbai, dreams of becoming a renowned actor. He lives with his widowed mother, Bela, and his friend Pappu Master in a small [chawl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chawl "Chawl"). Omi adores the glamorous superstar actress Shantipriya, often expressing his feelings in front of her film poster. One night, he and Pappu sneak into the premiere of Shanti's film, _Dreamy Girl_, in disguise, making a memorable impression on her. Later, Omi, inebriated, gives a heartfelt acceptance speech to Pappu and local children, pretending to have won an award.

Omi and Pappu land minor roles at R.C. Studios, owned by the egotistical producer Mukesh Mehra, who also launched Shanti's career. During a shoot, Shanti gets trapped in a fire but is rescued by Omi. The two become friends, and although Omi initially lies about being a [Tamil film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_cinema "Tamil cinema") star to impress her, he eventually confesses the truth. Shanti grows close to Omi, and with Pappu's help, they share a memorable evening date together at the studio.

Omi overhears a heated argument between Shanti and Mukesh, revealing that they are secretly married. Shanti is furious when she learns that Mukesh plans to marry the daughter of the distributor for his upcoming film, _Om Shanti Om_. She reveals to Mukesh that she is pregnant with his child, which seems to please him. Heartbroken, Omi avoids Shanti.

One night, Mukesh takes Shanti to the future set of _Om Shanti Om_, claiming he will cancel the film and have a grand wedding there to make their marriage public. Omi visits Shanti but is devastated to see her with Mukesh; he leaves without either noticing. However, once Omi leaves, Mukesh reveals his true colours to Shanti, confessing that his actual plan is to kill her and their unborn child to avoid any impedance in his career as a producer. He lights up the set on fire and locks Shanti inside. Despite his attempts to rescue her after Mukesh leaves, Omi gets beaten by Mukesh's guards and is thrown out by an explosion by the time he can get to Shanti. The set burns down with Shanti inside. Omi is later struck by the car of actor Rajesh Kapoor, whose wife Lovely is in labor. Rajesh brings Omi to the hospital, but he dies from his injuries, while Rajesh and Lovely welcome a baby boy named Om Kapoor.

30 years later, Om Kapoor aka O. K., now a successful yet arrogant actor, suffers from [pyrophobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrophobia "Pyrophobia") and frequently encounters Bela, who believes him to be her son. He dismisses her as delusional, and Pappu, now old, tries to explain the truth, but Bela remains unconvinced.

While shooting at the abandoned R.C. Studios, O.K. experiences vivid flashbacks of Omi trying to rescue Shanti and later unwittingly delivers Omi's old drunken speech at a [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") event. Pappu watches him on TV and realizes that Omi has reincarnated as Om Kapoor. At a party celebrating his victory, O.K. meets Mukesh, now known as Mike, who proposes a film collaboration; an introduction to him causes O.K. to fully remember his previous life. Om finally reunites with Bela and Pappu at the old chawl, and together with Om's assistant Anwar, they plan to expose Mukesh's crimes.

O.K. resumes filming _Om Shanti Om_ at the old studio after convincing Mukesh to revive the project, and after many failed auditions of other actresses, hires Sandhya "Sandy" Bansal, an aspiring actress who is an exact doppelgänger of Shanti and a huge fangirl of Om. Pappu and Bela start training her to behave exactly like Shanti. Om initially hides his plan but later reveals the truth to Sandy, who promises to help him. At the film's inauguration, Bela, disguised as a witch, and Sandy, disguised as Shanti's ghost, try to scare Mukesh into confessing. Despite a fake inauguration plan gone wrong, a photograph of Shanti inexplicably catches fire, unsettling Mukesh and confusing Om and Pappu.

During a masquerade ball for the film's music launch, Om indirectly hints at Mukesh's guilt through Shanti's story. However, Sandy accidentally reveals her ruse by injuring herself, proving she is not a ghost. Mukesh, suspicious of the film reels, chases Sandy but is knocked out by a chandelier. When he regains consciousness, O.K. confronts him in the empty venue about Shanti's murder. Mukesh mocks O.K., claiming there is no proof and revealing he knows Sandy is not Shanti. Sandy then appears, disclosing that Mukesh had buried Shanti alive under the chandelier after discovering she had survived the initial fire. She even foretells that Shanti's body will be found, which will be proof of murder for the court. Both Om and Mukesh are perturbed at how deeply she knows Shanti's tragic story; in the confrontation that follows, Om finally overcomes his pyrophobia and defeats Mukesh, who is crushed to death by the falling chandelier.

Pappu and Anwar arrive with the real Sandy. Om then realizes that the woman with him is actually Shanti's ghost, who was also responsible for the unexplained aids in his plan. With her death now avenged, Om and Shanti bid each other a tearful goodbye, and he reunites with Sandy while Shanti runs up the stairs and disappears, having attained peace.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Development")]

In 2002, [Farah Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farah_Khan "Farah Khan") worked as a choreographer for the musical _[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ in London, which she felt presented a "clichéd and outdated version" of the Indian film industry.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) She thought that the musical would not be successful if released in India.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) She instead thought of a new story, writing her initial thoughts about the subject on [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber")'s letterhead while staying in his house.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-9) Later in 2006, Farah began to work on her next project, which was tentatively titled _Happy New Year_. Amid speculations that [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") would star in _Happy New Year_, the actor rejected the first draft of the film, upon which Farah's husband and editor [Shirish Kunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirish_Kunder "Shirish Kunder") reminded her of the story she had conceived while in London.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10)_Happy New Year_, which was to mark [Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone")'s Hindi debut, was put on hiatus and revived more than 8 years later under the [same title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_New_Year_(2014_film) "Happy New Year (2014 film)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-11)

Farah completed writing the first script of _Om Shanti Om_ within two weeks.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-12) She set the first half in the 1970s as she felt the [Hindi films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") made during that period were much more influential than those made in other periods, particularly the 1980s, which she felt was a period when "the worst movies were made". She also included many references to the 1970s, which were also prevalent in films of that time. She said, "Everything in the first half is about the 70s—such as the mother who overacts, mouthing clichéd dialogues. Then there are cabarets, badminton and other stuff popular during that era."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) Shah Rukh's costumes were designed by [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar"), while [Manish Malhotra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manish_Malhotra "Manish Malhotra") designed Padukone's costumes. The rest of the cast had their costumes designed by Sanjeev Mulchandani.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-13)

In addition to directing the film, Farah co-wrote the story with [Mayur Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayur_Puri "Mayur Puri") and [Mushtaq Shiekh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushtaq_Shiekh "Mushtaq Shiekh"). She was also the film's choreographer. Puri wrote the screenplay and dialogues.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14) He completed the writing process in two months and rewrote the film's second half.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-15) Puri created the screenplay by writing his natural reaction to the characters as scenarios. He knew that despite being part of a crowd, junior artists do not want to be recognised as such, ruins their chances of landing a leading role in future. This was used in a sequence involving Shah Rukh and Talpade, who play junior artists. Puri blended different genres together in _Om Shanti Om_, which he felt was challenging. He used his personal memories from childhood for creating the 1970s.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-comic-16) Shirish Kunder was the editor, while V. Manikandan was the cinematographer.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14)

[Sabu Cyril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabu_Cyril "Sabu Cyril") was the film's [production designer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Production_designer "Production designer"). Sabu was first offered the [Mani Ratnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mani_Ratnam "Mani Ratnam")-directed _[Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guru\_(2007\_film) "Guru (2007 film)")_ (2007) at a time when _Om Shanti Om_ was being planned, but ultimately chosen the latter due to his earlier commitment to Farah for her future project.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-17) Farah used two particular dialogues in the film: "When you want something badly, the whole universe conspires to give to you" and "In the end everything will be ok and if its not ok its not the end". These were used as Khan felt that it reflected her philosophy in her life.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-18) Farah stated that the film's opening scene was her most favourite in it.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-19) In 2008, Puri felt his most favourite dialogue from the ones he wrote would be the Filmfare Awards speech.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-comic-16) The film's title derives from the eponymous song from the film _[Karz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karz\_(film) "Karz (film)")_ (1980).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-20)[Om](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om "Om") is a Hindu mantra; _Om Shanti Om_ roughly translates to "Peace Be With You".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-22)

The film opens with the grandeur shot of the most famous songs of _Karz_ that is _Om Shanti Om_ featuring [Rishi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rishi_Kapoor "Rishi Kapoor") and [SRK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SRK "SRK") as a junior film artist standing in the crowd.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-23)

### Casting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Casting")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Deepika_Padukone_promoting_RACE_2_on_NACH_BALIYE_5.jpg/250px-Deepika_Padukone_promoting_RACE_2_on_NACH_BALIYE_5.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Deepika_Padukone_promoting_RACE_2_on_NACH_BALIYE_5.jpg)

[Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone") plays the love interest of Shah Rukh Khan's character in her Hindi film debut.

Shah Rukh was cast as the lead; he worked hard on his physique for a song sequence.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-24) He felt _Om Shanti Om_ was a "happy film".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-25)

Farah was advised by [Malaika Arora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaika_Arora "Malaika Arora") to cast Padukone as the female lead, who was suggested by [Wendell Rodricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendell_Rodricks "Wendell Rodricks"), under whom Padukone was working.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-26) She was cast without a screen test.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-27) Khan felt that she was "a beautiful, classic Indian beauty" who fit the role of an actor of the 1970s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-hate-8) She was excited at the prospect of working with Shah Rukh and said, "I've grown up watching [Shah Rukh] and always admired him so much. To get to work with him... is quite wonderful. It was also fantastic that Farah showed faith in my talent and cast me opposite him."[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-28)

In preparation for her role, Padukone watched several films of actresses [Helen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_(actress) "Helen (actress)") and [Hema Malini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") to study their body language.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-29) Her character was modelled after Malini and nicknamed Dreamy Girl after her the latter's nickname as Dream Girl.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-30) Rampal was approached by both Khan and Shah Rukh at the latter's New Year's Eve party. Rampal was initially reluctant to do the role as he felt it was "too evil" for someone like him. With persuasion from Shah Rukh, he agreed. Rampal wore a mustache in the film which was suggested by Shah Rukh.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10) Shreyas Talpade played a supporting role as the best friend of Khan's character. After the release of _Iqbal_ (2005) and completing the filming of _Dor_, Talpade, who attended the same gym as Khan, was called for a narration of what would be _Om Shanti Om_. He agreed to do the role.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-late-31)

[Kirron Kher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirron_Kher "Kirron Kher"), [Bindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bindu_(actress) "Bindu (actress)") and [Javed Sheikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javed_Sheikh "Javed Sheikh") also appear in the film.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BOI_OSO_Cast-32) A further red carpet scene featuring a number of actors making guest appearances, including [R. Madhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._Madhavan "R. Madhavan") and [Farhan Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar") as well as [Prem Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Chopra "Prem Chopra"), [Shakti Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Kapoor "Shakti Kapoor") and [Vidhu Vinod Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidhu_Vinod_Chopra "Vidhu Vinod Chopra") was deleted from the film.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-33)

### Principal photography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Principal photography")]

_Om Shanti Om_ was made on a budget of ₹40 crore.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BOI-2) The first scene to be filmed was one where Talpade's character tells Shah Rukh's character that he will be a hero; Shah Rukh was an hour late for filming.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-late-31) Farah was pregnant with triplets while filming and experienced difficulties while shooting, she would constantly vomit while directing the film.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-34) The film was shot entirely in sync sound; Farah dismissed rumours of Padukone's voice being dubbed.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-35) In 2015, however, [Mona Ghosh Shetty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mona_Ghosh_Shetty "Mona Ghosh Shetty") admitted to have dubbed for Padukone in the film.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-36) The fake fight scene involving a stuffed tiger was inspired by a similar scene in the film _Tarzan 303_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10) Old cars owned by actors [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") and [Hema Malini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hema_Malini "Hema Malini") were used for filming for authenticity.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-mtv-37)

A number of references to real life was also filmed, including a scene in which Om rescues Shanti from a fire, which was a spoof of [Sunil Dutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Dutt "Sunil Dutt") rescuing [Nargis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nargis "Nargis") from a fire on the sets of _[Mother India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother\_India "Mother India")_ (1957). For a shot involving a Filmfare Awards ceremony, Khan stood on the red carpet of an actual Filmfare Award ceremony and requested actors to dictate dialogues as she stated. The song "Dhoom Taana" has digitally altered guest appearances, which included [Sunil Dutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunil_Dutt "Sunil Dutt") from _[Amrapali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrapali\_(film) "Amrapali (film)")_ (1966), [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") from _[Sachaa Jhutha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachaa\_Jhutha "Sachaa Jhutha")_ (1970) and [Jeetendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeetendra "Jeetendra") from _[Jay Vejay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay\_Vejay "Jay Vejay")_ (1977).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-38) Farah wanted to film [Shakira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakira "Shakira") for filming a special appearance had made her commit a few days for the role. Due to the uncertainty of her dates, the idea was scrapped.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-mtv-37)

In February 2007, a filming schedule was completed in Film City. It was then reported that filming would move outdoors after Shah Rukh completed filming for _[Kaun Banega Crorepati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaun\_Banega\_Crorepati "Kaun Banega Crorepati")_.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-39) The visuals of the song "Deewangi Deewangi" where Om meets Mukesh, was heavily inspired by a scene featuring [Jeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeet_(actor) "Jeet (actor)") and [Priyanshu Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priyanshu_Chatterjee "Priyanshu Chatterjee") from [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language") film _Bidhatar Lekha_, which was also based on the theme of reincarnation and coincidentally was released in April 2007.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-40) It was shot over a period of six days.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-i-10) In October 2007, [Abhishek Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhishek_Bachchan "Abhishek Bachchan") finished filming for his cameo appearance; he shot between 10 and 2 in the night for his screen time of about one and a half minutes.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-41) Filming of the last sequence and the end-credit song was done in [Film City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_City,_Mumbai "Film City, Mumbai").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-42) Farah continued the tradition of featuring an end-credits song beginning with _[Main Hoon Na](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main\_Hoon\_Na "Main Hoon Na")_ (2004).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-43)

_Om Shanti Om_ was produced by Shah Rukh's wife [Gauri Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauri_Khan "Gauri Khan") under their [Red Chillies Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment") banner. While Marching Ants handled the publicity design, Gauri was the presenter. Shyam Kaushal, Amar Shetty and Shah Rukh were the action directors.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14) The film's final reel length was 4013.94 ft (1223.45 m).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-BH_Cast-14)

## Release

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Release")]

### Theatrical

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Theatrical")]

#### Screening and statics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Screening and statics")]

_Om Shanti Om_ created a record of sorts by going in for an unheard of 2000 prints (worldwide) release. This was the highest number of prints (including digital) for any Indian movie at the time of its release.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-AGNIBAAN-50)

#### Pre-sale records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Om_Shanti_Om&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Pre-sale records")]

_Om Shanti Om_ set another record for registered pre-advance booking of 18,000 tickets in a chain of theatres in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") a few days before the advance booking was to start.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-Record_Pre_Advance_Booking-51) A special screening was conducted for Bollywood actors.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-sify.com-52)[Red Chillies Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Chillies_Entertainment "Red Chillies Entertainment") had reportedly sold the world rights for the film to [Eros International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eros_Labs "Eros Labs") for an amount between Rs. 720–750 million. Baba Films, a production and distribution company, had offered a record Rs. 110 million for the rights to the Mumbai Circuit, surpassing the highest amount ever paid for the territory. As a marketing strategy, Amul advertised Shah Rukh.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om#cite_note-53)

### Home media
