_**White Mischief**_ is a 1987 British [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama")[crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama") film directed and co-written by Michael Radford. It dramatises the events of the [Happy Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_Valley_set "Happy Valley set") murder case in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") in 1941, wherein Sir [Henry “Jock” Delves Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jock_Delves_Broughton "Jock Delves Broughton") was tried for the murder of [Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josslyn_Hay,_22nd_Earl_of_Erroll "Josslyn Hay, 22nd Earl of Erroll"). The film stars [Greta Scacchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Scacchi "Greta Scacchi"), [Charles Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Dance "Charles Dance"), [Joss Ackland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joss_Ackland "Joss Ackland"), [Sarah Miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Miles "Sarah Miles"), [Geraldine Chaplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geraldine_Chaplin "Geraldine Chaplin"), [Ray McAnally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_McAnally "Ray McAnally"), [Murray Head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murray_Head "Murray Head"), [John Hurt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hurt "John Hurt"), and [Trevor Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Howard "Trevor Howard").

The screenplay is based on the non-fiction book _[White Mischief: The Murder of Lord Erroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White\_Mischief\_(novel) "White Mischief (novel)")_ (1982), by [James Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fox_(journalist) "James Fox (journalist)"), which originated from a newspaper article published in 1969.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-whitemischief-6) Shooting took place on-location in Kenya and at [Shepperton Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepperton_Studios "Shepperton Studios").

At the [42nd British Academy Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/42nd_British_Academy_Film_Awards "42nd British Academy Film Awards"), the film was nominated for [Best Actor in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role") (for Joss Ackland) and [Best Costume Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Costume_Design "BAFTA Award for Best Costume Design").

The film came out around the same time as a BBC series set against the background of the same crime, _[The Happy Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Happy\_Valley "The Happy Valley")_ (1987).

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

Throughout the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), aristocrats in the [Kenya Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Colony "Kenya Colony")'s Happy Valley region often led hedonistic lifestyles of indulgence in alcohol, drugs, and extramarital relationships. On 24 January 1941, Josslyn Hay, the philandering Earl of Erroll, was found dead in his car in a secluded area, with his reputation for adulterous relationships preceding him.

One such married woman is [Diana Delves Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Caldwell "Diana Caldwell"), the beautiful wife of Sir John Henry Delves Broughton, known as "Jock", who is thirty years her senior, with whom she has a pre-nuptial understanding that, should either of them fall in love with someone else, the other party would not impede that romance.

Diana has indeed succumbed to the charms of the Earl of Erroll,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-jongh-7) whose other lovers include the drug-addicted American heiress [Alice de Janzé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_de_Janz%C3%A9 "Alice de Janzé") and the more reserved Nina Soames. The Earl is more serious about this affair than any of his earlier dalliances, and wants Diana to marry him. She is reluctant to leave what she thinks is the financial security of her marriage to formalise her relationship with Erroll (who has no funds or prospects), unaware that her husband is deep in debt. Privately humiliated but appearing to honour their agreement, Delves Broughton publicly toasts the couple's affair at the club in Nairobi, asking Erroll to bring Diana home at a specified time. Delves Broughton appears to be extremely intoxicated for the rest of the evening; once he is alone it is clear he was feigning drunkenness. After dropping off Diana, Erroll is shot dead in his car near the home of Delves Broughton, who is soon charged with the murder.

Diana is distraught over losing her lover, as is Alice, who openly masturbates next to his corpse at the mortuary. A local plantation owner, Gilbert Colvile, whose only friend is Delves Broughton, quietly offers Diana advice and solace and ultimately shocks her by proposing marriage.

Delves Broughton stands trial. There are no witnesses to the crime and the physical evidence that appears incriminating is also circumstantial. He obviously had the motive and means, but is found innocent, and the scandal comes to an end. De Janzé ultimately kills herself, and Diana discovers further evidence that implicates her husband in her lover's death. After killing their dog and then menacing her with a shotgun, Broughton shoots himself in front of her. The film ends with a fleeing, bloodstained Diana discovering the remaining Happy Valley set partying around de Janzé's grave.

## Original book

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Original book")]

In 1969, James Fox and [Cyril Connolly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyril_Connolly "Cyril Connolly") began investigating the case for an article in _The Sunday Times_ called "Christmas at Karen." After Connolly died in 1974, Fox inherited his notes and theories, and returned to Kenya to undertake further research. The result was the book _White Mischief_, published in 1982.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-8)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-sight-3) The title came from _[Black Mischief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Mischief "Black Mischief")_, [Evelyn Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh "Evelyn Waugh")'s satirical novel set in the mythical African kingdom of Azania. _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ called it "a fascinating book."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-9)_[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ said "had ‘White Mischief’ been a work of fiction it would have required the collaboration of [Agatha Christie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agatha_Christie "Agatha Christie") and [P. G. Wodehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._G._Wodehouse "P. G. Wodehouse")."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-10) While researching the book Fox also collected information about [Beryl Markham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl_Markham "Beryl Markham"), which was turned into the film _[A Shadow on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beryl\_Markham:\_A\_Shadow\_on\_the\_Sun "Beryl Markham: A Shadow on the Sun")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-11)

## Development

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")]

The film rights to the book were optioned by [Michael White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_White_(producer) "Michael White (producer)"), a friend of Fox's, while the book was being written.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-12)

Director Michael Radford collaborated with British playwright Jonathan Gems on the script. Radford emphasized that "films of [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") should be made by Africans" and described the project as "a film of melancholy about people who have everything and yet have nothing. It's about people who want to possess what they can't possess."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-csm-13)

Securing funding for the film posed a challenge. The financing was sourced from a chain of Canadian cinemas, [Cineplex Odeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cineplex_Odeon_Corporation "Cineplex Odeon Corporation"), plus [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-ink-14), BBC Television, [Nelson Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Entertainment "Nelson Entertainment") (headed by [Barry Spikings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Spikings "Barry Spikings"), which provided $2.5 million in exchange for North American video rights), with the remaining amount coming from [Columbia Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Pictures "Columbia Pictures"), then under [David Puttnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Puttnam "David Puttnam") as head of production.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-white-2)

[Richard Attenborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Attenborough "Richard Attenborough") was offered and turned down the lead role, because he wanted to focus on directing films.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-15)

## Shooting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Shooting")]

Filming took place from February to May 1987 at [Shepperton Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shepperton_Studios "Shepperton Studios") and on location in Kenya.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-16)[Wrotham Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrotham_Park "Wrotham Park") was used as [Doddington Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doddington_Hall,_Cheshire "Doddington Hall, Cheshire"), the home of Delves Broughton.

## Historical accuracy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Historical accuracy")]

The real Alice De Janzé shot herself on 30 September 1941,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-17) while Jock Delves Broughton eventually returned to England and committed suicide by [morphine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphine "Morphine") overdose in the [Adelphi Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Adelphi_Hotel "Britannia Adelphi Hotel") in [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") in December 1942, over a year later.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-18)

"There is a difference between fact and truth," said producer Simon Perry. "You can be truthful without being factual. It's inevitable there will be people who think Kenya was and still is a paradise of [remittance men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remittance_man "Remittance man") and black sheep of aristocratic families. Kenya was an exaggerated microcosm of society in Britain at that time, painted in primary colours with characters larger than life."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-csm-13)

Sir Jock Broughton's son, Sir Evelyn, complained that the film depicted his father as a murderer. He said his father was too drunk that night to have committed the crime and that Diana was more likely to have done it.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-19)

Diana Broughton died in 1987.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-20)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Reception")]

### Box office

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Box office")]

The film grossed £1,532,903 in the United Kingdom and $3.1 million in the United States and Canada.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-screen-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-mojo-5) It lost money during its theatrical release, however, [Jake Eberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Eberts "Jake Eberts") reported that [Goldcrest Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goldcrest_Films "Goldcrest Films") invested £1,300,000 in the film, and received £1,633,000, earning them a profit of £333,000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-screen-4)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-23)

### Critical

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical")]

_[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety\_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")_ wrote the film "displays high production values, impressive acting talent, and a strong — virtually factual — storyline. The money invested can be seen on the screen, and with an excellent lead performance (following his major role in ‘‘The Sicilian’’) Joss Ackland should finally receive the acting kudos he deserves. Pic should make a healthy b.o. impact worldwide."[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-24)

Book author James Fox said he was "ambivalent" about the movie.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-jongh-7)

Radford said the reviews of the film " almost ruined my career. It stopped it in its tracks... I think it was difficult for critics because Britain is obsessed by class. It wasn’t done to make a film about upper-class people. I think people were expecting one of those James Ivory films or _A Passage to India_... It wasn’t meant to be like _Out of Africa_, the cinema of waxed furniture. I was trying to make something much more decadent."[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-25)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=White_Mischief_(film)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 1996, [Mariette Bosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariette_Bosch "Mariette Bosch") murdered Ria Wolmerans in [Botswana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botswana "Botswana"). Both women were white South Africans. The case was referred to as "Botswana's white mischief".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Mischief_(film)#cite_note-BarrowBBC-26)

**Shekhar Kulbhushan Kapur** (born 6 December 1945) is an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_people "Indian people") filmmaker.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1) Born into the [Anand-Sahni family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand-Sahni_family "Anand-Sahni family"), Kapur is the recipient of several accolades, including a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"), a [National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award "National Film Award"), a [National Board of Review Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review") and three [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), in addition to nomination for a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award").

Kapur became known in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") with his recurring role in the television series _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandaan\_(TV\_series) "Khandaan (TV series)")_. He then made his directorial debut with [cult classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following")_[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ in 1983, before gaining widespread acclaim with _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ in 1987. He then gained international recognition and acclaim in 1994 with [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film") film _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, based on the infamous [Indian bandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacoity "Dacoity") and politician [Phoolan Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoolan_Devi "Phoolan Devi"). The film premiered in the directors' fortnight section of the [1994 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Cannes_Film_Festival "1994 Cannes Film Festival") and was screened at the [Edinburgh Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Festival_Fringe "Edinburgh Festival Fringe").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)

Kapur achieved further international prominence with the 1998 period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictionalized account of the reign of [English Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England"), which was nominated for seven [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He then directed [war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_film "War film")[drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)")_[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_ (2002). In 2007, he directed _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, the sequel to his 1998 film.

Shekhar Kapur was awarded the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan"), India's third highest civilian award, in 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Balakrishna,_Ajith,_Shekhar_Kapur,_Shobana_honoured_with_Padma_Bhushan,_Arijit_Singh,_Ricky_Kej_conferred_with_Padma_Shri-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Shekhar was born on 6 December 1945 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"), [Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_(British_India) "Punjab (British India)"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_India "British India"), in a [Punjabi Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu") family to Kulbhushan Kapoor, a doctor with a flourishing practice, and his wife Sheel Kanta Kapoor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1)

Whilst travelling on a train from the newly created Pakistan to India, a massacre took place; Kapur's mother Sheel played dead and hid both him and his sister under her body.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5) Reflecting on this, Kapur stated that the [partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") happened through "the blood of one people".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5)

The nephew of famous Indian actor [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") (Kapur's mother Sheel Kanta was the sister of actors [Chetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)"), Dev and [Vijay Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay_Anand_(Hindi_film_maker) "Vijay Anand (Hindi film maker)")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-6)), he was discouraged from getting into films by his father.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-NYT-7) Kapur is the only son of his parents and he has three sisters. One of his sisters, Neelu, was the first wife of actor [Navin Nischol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navin_Nischol "Navin Nischol"), while another sister, Aruna, is the wife of actor [Parikshit Sahni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parikshit_Sahni "Parikshit Sahni"). His third and youngest sister is [Sohaila Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sohaila_Kapur "Sohaila Kapur").

Kapur attended [Modern School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_School_(New_Delhi) "Modern School (New Delhi)") of [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-8) He studied economics at [St. Stephen's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Stephen's_College,_Delhi "St. Stephen's College, Delhi"). At 22, he became a [Chartered Accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chartered_Accountant "Chartered Accountant") with the [ICAEW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Chartered_Accountants_in_England_and_Wales "Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales") in England, having studied accountancy at the behest of his parents.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-10) He then started his career working with a multinational oil company. He moved to the United Kingdom in 1970, and spent several years working as an accountant and [management consultant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management_consultant "Management consultant").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-11)

## Filmmaking career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Filmmaking career")]

### In India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: In India")]

He turned director with the family drama _[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ (1983), starring [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah"), [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi") and a young [Jugal Hansraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jugal_Hansraj "Jugal Hansraj") and [Urmila Matondkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar "Urmila Matondkar"). The plot followed the story of an illegitimate boy who struggles to find acceptance from his stepmother. He then directed the 1987 science-fiction film _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_, starring [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Amrish Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrish_Puri "Amrish Puri") in his most famous role as the villain Mogambo. Puri's most famous dialogue in this film "Mogambo Khush Hua" is still remembered.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-12) In 1994 he directed the critically acclaimed _Bandit Queen_[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-13) and played a cameo in the film as a truck driver.

Kapur was infamous for abandoning several films in which he was originally the director.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-14) He was originally the director of the 1989 film _[Joshilaay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshilaay "Joshilaay")_, which starred [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Meenakshi Sheshadri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Sheshadri "Meenakshi Sheshadri") before leaving the production halfway, and its producer Sibti Hassan Rizvi stepped in to complete the film. In 1992, he had shot some scenes for _[Barsaat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barsaat\_(1995\_film) "Barsaat (1995 film)")_, which was originally titled _Champion_[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-15) and was going to be the debut film of [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol"), but he left the production and was replaced by [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi"). In 1995, he partly directed _[Dushmani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushmani:\_A\_Violent\_Love\_Story "Dushmani: A Violent Love Story")_, starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala") before its producer Bunty Soorma stepped in to complete the film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-16)

Kapur was the executive producer of the film _[The Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guru\_(2002\_film) "The Guru (2002 film)")_. He established an Indian film company with [Ram Gopal Verma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Gopal_Verma "Ram Gopal Verma") and Mani Ratnam, though the group has thus far produced only one film, _[Dil Se..](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se.. "Dil Se..")_ (1998), starring [Shahrukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala"). Kapur executive-produced the [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood")-themed [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theatre "Musical theatre")_[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ by [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber"), which ran in London's [the West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") and on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") in New York City for 1 year.

In 2016, Kapur delivers an autobiographical film and documentary about [Amma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi "Mata Amritanandamayi"), well known as [Mata Amritanandamayi Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi_Devi "Mata Amritanandamayi Devi"), called "The Science of Compassion".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-17)

### International

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: International")]

In 1998, he received international recognition for the second time after _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, when he directed the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award")-winning period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictional account of the reign of [British Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England") nominated for seven [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). The 2007 sequel, _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, was nominated for two [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He was accused of being anti-British by [British tabloids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_tabloid "British tabloid") for his inaccurate portrayal of the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") in the 2002 movie _[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_. He denied the accusations and stated that he was merely "anti-colonisation".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-18)

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

Kapur started his career as an actor in the movie _[Jaan Hazir Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaan\_Hazir\_Hai "Jaan Hazir Hai")_ (1975)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-19) starring [Prem Kishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Kishen "Prem Kishen") and [Trilok Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilok_Kapoor "Trilok Kapoor") and later in _[Toote Khilone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toote\_Khilone "Toote Khilone")_, in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood"). He appeared in several Hindi television dramas, such as _[Udaan (Doordarshan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udaan\_(1989\_TV\_series) "Udaan (1989 TV series)")_, opposite [Kavita Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavita_Chaudhary "Kavita Chaudhary"), _Upanyaas_[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-20) (Doordarshan) opposite Nisha Singh, and _Masoom_ opposite Neena Gupta.

He served as judge on the reality TV series _[India's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India's\_Got\_Talent "India's Got Talent")_, aired on [Colors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colors_TV "Colors TV").

In an unusual role for him, Kapur provided the voice of [Mohandas Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohandas_Gandhi "Mohandas Gandhi") in the [Charkha Audiobooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charkha_Audiobooks "Charkha Audiobooks") title of _[The Story of My Experiments with Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Story\_of\_My\_Experiments\_with\_Truth "The Story of My Experiments with Truth")_, alongside [Nandita Das](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandita_Das "Nandita Das") as narrator.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2013, Kapur hosted the TV show _[Pradhanmantri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pradhanmantri\_(TV\_Series) "Pradhanmantri (TV Series)")_ on [ABP News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABP_News "ABP News"). On the show, which aims to bring never-seen-before facets of Indian history, he was the narrator.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-21)

### Comic book publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Comic book publishing")]

Further information: [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics")

In 2006, Kapur formed [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics") and Virgin Animation, an entertainment company focused on creating new stories and characters for a global audience. The [Shakti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Comics#Shakti "Virgin Comics") titles of Kapur and [Deepak Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak_Chopra "Deepak Chopra")'s company debuted with _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(comics) "Devi (comics)")_ and _[The Sadhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sadhu "The Sadhu")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)_Devi_ is about "a fierce feminine warrior, stronger than the Gods themselves ... a champion of the heavens, and the protector of man", while _The Sadhu_ "is about one man's choice between his spiritual oath and his human instinct."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kapur had a relationship for seven years with actress [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-23) He first was married to Medha Gujral, niece of former Indian Prime Minister [Inder Kumar Gujral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inder_Kumar_Gujral "Inder Kumar Gujral").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-24) They divorced in 1994.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-25) She died on 25 November 2014 at a hospital in New York City of liver failure following a second heart and first kidney transplant.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-26) Kapur later married actress [Suchitra Krishnamoorthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suchitra_Krishnamoorthi "Suchitra Krishnamoorthi") in 1999.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-27) They have a daughter named Kaveri Kapur.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-28) The couple divorced in 2007.

In March 2020, Krishnamoorthi filed a case against Kapur over a property dispute concerning their daughter Kaveri.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-29) She claimed that the property rightfully belongs to their daughter, but has been rented to actor [Kabir Bedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir_Bedi "Kabir Bedi") and his wife Parveen.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-30)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

In 2000, he received [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri"), the fourth highest civilian award in India.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Padma_Awards-31) In 2010, he served as one of the Jury Members in international competition at the [63rd Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Cannes_Film_Festival "2010 Cannes Film Festival").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-hollywoodreporter-32) In 2020, Kapur became the president of the [Film and Television Institute of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_and_Television_Institute_of_India "Film and Television Institute of India").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-33)

In 2023, Kapur served as the chairperson of the International competition Jury at the [54th International Film Festival of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_International_Film_Festival_of_India "54th International Film Festival of India") held from 20 November to 28 November.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-34)

**Shekhar Kulbhushan Kapur** (born 6 December 1945) is an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_people "Indian people") filmmaker.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1) Born into the [Anand-Sahni family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand-Sahni_family "Anand-Sahni family"), Kapur is the recipient of several accolades, including a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards"), a [National Film Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award "National Film Award"), a [National Board of Review Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review "National Board of Review") and three [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"), in addition to nomination for a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award").

Kapur became known in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") with his recurring role in the television series _[Khandaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khandaan\_(TV\_series) "Khandaan (TV series)")_. He then made his directorial debut with [cult classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following")_[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ in 1983, before gaining widespread acclaim with _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ in 1987. He then gained international recognition and acclaim in 1994 with [biographical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film") film _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, based on the infamous [Indian bandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacoity "Dacoity") and politician [Phoolan Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoolan_Devi "Phoolan Devi"). The film premiered in the directors' fortnight section of the [1994 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Cannes_Film_Festival "1994 Cannes Film Festival") and was screened at the [Edinburgh Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Festival_Fringe "Edinburgh Festival Fringe").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)

Kapur achieved further international prominence with the 1998 period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictionalized account of the reign of [English Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England"), which was nominated for seven [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He then directed [war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_film "War film")[drama film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)")_[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_ (2002). In 2007, he directed _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, the sequel to his 1998 film.

Shekhar Kapur was awarded the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan"), India's third highest civilian award, in 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Balakrishna,_Ajith,_Shekhar_Kapur,_Shobana_honoured_with_Padma_Bhushan,_Arijit_Singh,_Ricky_Kej_conferred_with_Padma_Shri-4)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Shekhar was born on 6 December 1945 in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"), [Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_(British_India) "Punjab (British India)"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_India "British India"), in a [Punjabi Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu") family to Kulbhushan Kapoor, a doctor with a flourishing practice, and his wife Sheel Kanta Kapoor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-TOI-1)

Whilst travelling on a train from the newly created Pakistan to India, a massacre took place; Kapur's mother Sheel played dead and hid both him and his sister under her body.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5) Reflecting on this, Kapur stated that the [partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") happened through "the blood of one people".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-HT2019-5)

The nephew of famous Indian actor [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand") (Kapur's mother Sheel Kanta was the sister of actors [Chetan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)"), Dev and [Vijay Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijay_Anand_(Hindi_film_maker) "Vijay Anand (Hindi film maker)")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-6)), he was discouraged from getting into films by his father.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-NYT-7) Kapur is the only son of his parents and he has three sisters. One of his sisters, Neelu, was the first wife of actor [Navin Nischol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navin_Nischol "Navin Nischol"), while another sister, Aruna, is the wife of actor [Parikshit Sahni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parikshit_Sahni "Parikshit Sahni"). His third and youngest sister is [Sohaila Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sohaila_Kapur "Sohaila Kapur").

Kapur attended [Modern School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_School_(New_Delhi) "Modern School (New Delhi)") of [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-8) He studied economics at [St. Stephen's College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Stephen's_College,_Delhi "St. Stephen's College, Delhi"). At 22, he became a [Chartered Accountant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chartered_Accountant "Chartered Accountant") with the [ICAEW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Chartered_Accountants_in_England_and_Wales "Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales") in England, having studied accountancy at the behest of his parents.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-10) He then started his career working with a multinational oil company. He moved to the United Kingdom in 1970, and spent several years working as an accountant and [management consultant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Management_consultant "Management consultant").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-11)

## Filmmaking career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Filmmaking career")]

### In India

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: In India")]

He turned director with the family drama _[Masoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masoom\_(1983\_film) "Masoom (1983 film)")_ (1983), starring [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah"), [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi") and a young [Jugal Hansraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jugal_Hansraj "Jugal Hansraj") and [Urmila Matondkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urmila_Matondkar "Urmila Matondkar"). The plot followed the story of an illegitimate boy who struggles to find acceptance from his stepmother. He then directed the 1987 science-fiction film _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_, starring [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Amrish Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrish_Puri "Amrish Puri") in his most famous role as the villain Mogambo. Puri's most famous dialogue in this film "Mogambo Khush Hua" is still remembered.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-12) In 1994 he directed the critically acclaimed _Bandit Queen_[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-13) and played a cameo in the film as a truck driver.

Kapur was infamous for abandoning several films in which he was originally the director.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-14) He was originally the director of the 1989 film _[Joshilaay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joshilaay "Joshilaay")_, which starred [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor "Anil Kapoor"), [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and [Meenakshi Sheshadri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meenakshi_Sheshadri "Meenakshi Sheshadri") before leaving the production halfway, and its producer Sibti Hassan Rizvi stepped in to complete the film. In 1992, he had shot some scenes for _[Barsaat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barsaat\_(1995\_film) "Barsaat (1995 film)")_, which was originally titled _Champion_[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-15) and was going to be the debut film of [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol"), but he left the production and was replaced by [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi"). In 1995, he partly directed _[Dushmani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushmani:\_A\_Violent\_Love\_Story "Dushmani: A Violent Love Story")_, starring [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol"), [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala") before its producer Bunty Soorma stepped in to complete the film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-16)

Kapur was the executive producer of the film _[The Guru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guru\_(2002\_film) "The Guru (2002 film)")_. He established an Indian film company with [Ram Gopal Verma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Gopal_Verma "Ram Gopal Verma") and Mani Ratnam, though the group has thus far produced only one film, _[Dil Se..](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se.. "Dil Se..")_ (1998), starring [Shahrukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") and [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala"). Kapur executive-produced the [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood")-themed [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_theatre "Musical theatre")_[Bombay Dreams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay\_Dreams "Bombay Dreams")_ by [Andrew Lloyd Webber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Lloyd_Webber "Andrew Lloyd Webber"), which ran in London's [the West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") and on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") in New York City for 1 year.

In 2016, Kapur delivers an autobiographical film and documentary about [Amma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi "Mata Amritanandamayi"), well known as [Mata Amritanandamayi Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Amritanandamayi_Devi "Mata Amritanandamayi Devi"), called "The Science of Compassion".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-17)

### International

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: International")]

In 1998, he received international recognition for the second time after _[Bandit Queen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandit\_Queen "Bandit Queen")_, when he directed the [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award")-winning period film _[Elizabeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth\_(film) "Elizabeth (film)")_, a fictional account of the reign of [British Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I_of_England "Elizabeth I of England") nominated for seven [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). The 2007 sequel, _[Elizabeth: The Golden Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth:\_The\_Golden\_Age "Elizabeth: The Golden Age")_, was nominated for two [Oscars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards"). He was accused of being anti-British by [British tabloids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_tabloid "British tabloid") for his inaccurate portrayal of the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army") in the 2002 movie _[The Four Feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Four\_Feathers\_(2002\_film) "The Four Feathers (2002 film)")_. He denied the accusations and stated that he was merely "anti-colonisation".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-18)

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

Kapur started his career as an actor in the movie _[Jaan Hazir Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaan\_Hazir\_Hai "Jaan Hazir Hai")_ (1975)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-19) starring [Prem Kishen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Kishen "Prem Kishen") and [Trilok Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilok_Kapoor "Trilok Kapoor") and later in _[Toote Khilone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toote\_Khilone "Toote Khilone")_, in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood"). He appeared in several Hindi television dramas, such as _[Udaan (Doordarshan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Udaan\_(1989\_TV\_series) "Udaan (1989 TV series)")_, opposite [Kavita Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavita_Chaudhary "Kavita Chaudhary"), _Upanyaas_[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-20) (Doordarshan) opposite Nisha Singh, and _Masoom_ opposite Neena Gupta.

He served as judge on the reality TV series _[India's Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India's\_Got\_Talent "India's Got Talent")_, aired on [Colors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colors_TV "Colors TV").

In an unusual role for him, Kapur provided the voice of [Mohandas Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohandas_Gandhi "Mohandas Gandhi") in the [Charkha Audiobooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charkha_Audiobooks "Charkha Audiobooks") title of _[The Story of My Experiments with Truth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Story\_of\_My\_Experiments\_with\_Truth "The Story of My Experiments with Truth")_, alongside [Nandita Das](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandita_Das "Nandita Das") as narrator.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2013, Kapur hosted the TV show _[Pradhanmantri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pradhanmantri\_(TV\_Series) "Pradhanmantri (TV Series)")_ on [ABP News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ABP_News "ABP News"). On the show, which aims to bring never-seen-before facets of Indian history, he was the narrator.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-21)

### Comic book publishing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Comic book publishing")]

Further information: [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics")

In 2006, Kapur formed [Liquid Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liquid_Comics "Liquid Comics") and Virgin Animation, an entertainment company focused on creating new stories and characters for a global audience. The [Shakti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Comics#Shakti "Virgin Comics") titles of Kapur and [Deepak Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak_Chopra "Deepak Chopra")'s company debuted with _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(comics) "Devi (comics)")_ and _[The Sadhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sadhu "The Sadhu")_.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)_Devi_ is about "a fierce feminine warrior, stronger than the Gods themselves ... a champion of the heavens, and the protector of man", while _The Sadhu_ "is about one man's choice between his spiritual oath and his human instinct."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Changing-22)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Kapur had a relationship for seven years with actress [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-23) He first was married to Medha Gujral, niece of former Indian Prime Minister [Inder Kumar Gujral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inder_Kumar_Gujral "Inder Kumar Gujral").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-24) They divorced in 1994.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-25) She died on 25 November 2014 at a hospital in New York City of liver failure following a second heart and first kidney transplant.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-26) Kapur later married actress [Suchitra Krishnamoorthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suchitra_Krishnamoorthi "Suchitra Krishnamoorthi") in 1999.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-27) They have a daughter named Kaveri Kapur.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-28) The couple divorced in 2007.

In March 2020, Krishnamoorthi filed a case against Kapur over a property dispute concerning their daughter Kaveri.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-29) She claimed that the property rightfully belongs to their daughter, but has been rented to actor [Kabir Bedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir_Bedi "Kabir Bedi") and his wife Parveen.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-30)

## Awards and honours

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shekhar_Kapur&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Awards and honours")]

In 2000, he received [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri"), the fourth highest civilian award in India.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Padma_Awards-31) In 2010, he served as one of the Jury Members in international competition at the [63rd Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Cannes_Film_Festival "2010 Cannes Film Festival").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-Shekhar_Kapur,_exclusive_interview-3)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-hollywoodreporter-32) In 2020, Kapur became the president of the [Film and Television Institute of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Film_and_Television_Institute_of_India "Film and Television Institute of India").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-33)

In 2023, Kapur served as the chairperson of the International competition Jury at the [54th International Film Festival of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/54th_International_Film_Festival_of_India "54th International Film Festival of India") held from 20 November to 28 November.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur#cite_note-34)

Anurag Singh Kashyap (born 10 September 1972) is an Indian film director, producer and screenwriter. Kashyap made his directorial debut with as yet unreleased Paanch, with Kay Kay Menon as the lead. As a filmmaker, he is known for Black Friday (2004), a controversial and award-winning Hindi film about the 1993 Mumbai bombings, followed by No Smoking (2007), Dev D (2009), Gulaal (2009), That Girl in Yellow Boots (2011) and Gangs of Wasseypur (2012). As a screenwriter, he wrote the scripts for the Filmfare Award-winning Satya (1998) and the Academy Award-nominated Canadian film Water (2005). He founded his film production company, Anurag Kashyap Films Pvt. Ltd. in 2009.

Born on 21st May 1966 in Kolkata, Sujoy Ghosh is an Indian film writer, director, actor and producer who is well known for his critically acclaimed movies like Jhankar Beats, Kahaani, Ahalya and Badla.  
  
The film maker started the trend of multiplex movies in Bollywood with his directorial debut Jhankaar Beats in 2003 which went on to become a superhit. Ghosh's mystery thriller film Kahaani which released in the year 2012 was his path-breaking female lead movie for which he bagged many awards including a National Film Award for Best Screenplay and a Filmfare Award for Best Director. In 2016, his film Kahaani 2 was released which is a sequel to Kahaani. With his 15 minuter short film - Ahalya (2015), he started the trend of mainstream directors making digital short films.  
  
His latest crime-thriller Badla, starring Amitabh Bachchan and Taapsee Pannu received a widespread acclaim and emerged as the content film of the year for its nail-biting plot that left the audiences at the edge of their seats till the very last moment. This is his second film with Amitabh Bachchan, first being Aladin and second being the 2016 thriller film Te3n which was produced by Sujoy. Alongside writing and directing films, Sujoy also acts with the Bengali mystery-thriller Satyanweshi (2013) being his debut film as an actor where he played the role of Byomkesh Bakshi.  
  
Not many know but the popular phrase of the IPL team Kolkata Knight Riders - "Korbo Lorbo Jeetbo Re" was penned by Sujoy himself. With the quality driven content in his films, Sujoy Ghosh is one of the leading filmmakers in the country.

 His 1999 Romantic-Drama, Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam, starring heartthrob duo Salman-Aishwarya became one of the most critically cherished movies of the Genre.  #### [5. Mira Nair](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0619762/?ref_=ls_t_5) 

    *   Director
    *   Producer
    *   Actress

[Monsoon Wedding (2001)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0265343/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

Accomplished Film Director/Writer/Producer Mira Nair was born in India and educated at Delhi University and at Harvard. She began her film career as an actor and then turned to directing award-winning documentaries, including So Far From India and India Cabaret. Her debut feature film, Salaam Bombay! was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film in 1988; it won the Camera D'Or (for best first feature) and the Prix du Publique (for most popular entry) at the Cannes Film Festival and 25 other international awards. Her next film, Mississippi Masala, an interracial love story set in the American South and Uganda, starring Denzel Washington and Sarita Choudhury, won three awards at the Venice Film Festival including Best Screenplay and The Audience Choice Award. Subsequent films include The Perez Family (with Marisa Tomei, Anjelica Huston, Alfred Molina and Chazz Palminteri), about an exiled Cuban family in Miami; and the sensuous Kama Sutra: A Tale of Love, which she directed and co-wrote. Nair directed My Own Country based on Dr. Abraham Verghese's best-selling memoir about a young immigrant doctor dealing with the AIDS epidemic. Made in 1998, My Own Country starred Naveen Andrews, Glenne Headly, Marisa Tomei, Swoosie Kurtz, and Hal Holbrook, and was awarded the NAACP award for best fiction feature. Nair returned to the documentary form in August 1999 with The Laughing Club of India, which was awarded The Special Jury Prize in the Festival International de Programmes Audiovisuels 2000. In the summer of 2000, Nair shot Monsoon Wedding in 30 days, a story of a Punjabi wedding starring Naseeruddin Shah and an ensemble of Indian actors. Winner of the Golden Lion at the 2001 Venice Film Festival, Monsoon Wedding also won a Golden Globe nomination for Best Foreign Language Film and opened worldwide to tremendous critical and commercial acclaim. Nair's next feature was an HBO original film, Hysterical Blindness. Set in working class New Jersey in 1987, the film stars Uma Thurman, Juliette Lewis, Gena Rowlands. Thurman and Lewis play single women looking for love in all the wrong places, while Rowlands, who plays Thurman's mother, adds to her daughter's hysteria when she finds Mr. Right in Ben Gazarra. The film received great critical acclaim and the highest ratings for HBO, garnering an audience of 15 million, a Golden Globe for Uma Thurman, and 3 Emmy Awards. Following the tragic events of September 11, 2001, Nair joined a group of 11 renowned filmmakers, each commissioned to direct a film that was 11 minutes, 9 seconds and one frame long. Nair's film is a retelling of real events in the life of the Hamdani family in Queens, whose eldest son was missing after September 11, and was then accused by the media of being a terrorist. 11.09.01 is the true story of a mother's search for her son who did not return home on that fateful day. In May 2003, Nair helmed the Focus Features production of the Thackeray classic, Vanity Fair, a provocative period tale set in post-colonial England, in which Reese Witherspoon plays the lead, Becky Sharp. The film is scheduled to release in Fall 2004. Nair's upcoming projects include Tony Kushner's Homebody/Kabul for HBO, and Hari Kunzru's The Impressionist, and there are also plans to take Monsoon Wedding to Broadway. Mirabai Films is establishing an annual filmmaker's laboratory, Maisha, which will be dedicated to the support of visionary screenwriters and directors in East Africa and India. The first lab, which is only for screenwriters, will be launched in August 2005 in Kampala, Uganda.

 #### [6. Sriram Raghavan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1437189/?ref_=ls_t_6) 

    *   Writer
    *   Director
    *   Actor

[Andhadhun (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8108198/?ref_=ls_knf_6)

Sriram Raghavan is an Indian filmmaker who works in the Hindi film industry. He is regarded as a writer of neo-noir thrillers that fall under the action genre. He was brought up in Pune, where he attended St. Vincent's High School. He went to Fergusson College in Pune to study economics.  
  
After finishing college, Raghavan first wished to build a career in journalism. He took up a job at Stardust magazine but moved on to join the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) in Pune to pursue a course in direction.  
  
After completing his studies, Raghavan worked on a short feature, [Raman Raghav - A City, A Killer.](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt12331898/?ls) It was based on the crimes of Raman Raghav (a serial killer of Bombay) and his arrest. Raghavan cast [Raghubir Yadav](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0944834/?ls) to play the character of Raman. The feature was made on a low budget and was never released.  
  
Raghavan later started writing for television serials. He wrote several episodes of [Aahat (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2812214/?ls) and [C.I.D. (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0401916/?ls). He also wrote and directed an episode in First Kill.  
  
Raghavan's career took a new turn after [Ram Gopal Varma](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0890060/?ls) liked his work in [Raman Raghav - A City, A Killer.](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt12331898/?ls) and signed him up to direct [Ek Hasina Thi (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0352314/?ls). The film starred [Saif Ali Khan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451307/?ls) and [Urmila Matondkar](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007107/?ls) in the lead roles. This thriller received positive reviews from critics. It was shown at the New York Asian Film Festival.  
  
Raghavan's next directorial venture was another thriller, [Johnny Gaddaar (2007)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1077248/?ls). It was the debut film of [Neil Nitin Mukesh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1778703/?ls). The story revolves around a group of five individuals who want to make a fortune through a shortcut. But things go out of hand suddenly when one of the group members gets killed, and the money he was holding goes missing. Though the film wasn't a commercial success, it succeeded in impressing the critics.  
  
In 2012, Raghavan released his third film, [Agent Vinod (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1395025/?ls), a spy thriller starring [Kareena Kapoor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004626/?ls) and [Saif Ali Khan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0451307/?ls). The story revolves around the secret mission of Agent Vinod to discover the reason behind his colleague's death. The film received mixed reviews from critics and failed to make a mark at the box office.  
  
Raghavan's fourth film was [Badlapur (2015)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3678782/?ls), a revenge action thriller that features [Varun Dhawan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3315894/?ls), [Nawazuddin Siddiqui](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1596350/?ls), and [Yami Gautam](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4417069/?ls) in lead roles. The storyline is based on Death's Dark Abyss, a novel written by Massimo Carlotto. The story is based on the theme of revenge and shows a devastated man out to avenge the death of his family. The movie got positive reviews from critics. It also earned him a nomination for Best Director at the 61st Filmfare awards.  
  
Raghavan explored the genre of black comedy in his crime thriller [Andhadhun (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8108198/?ls). The film stars [Ayushmann Khurrana](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4731677/?ls), [Tabu](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0007102/?ls), and [Radhika Apte](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2331000/?ls). The movie's storyline revolves around a blind piano player involved in the murder of a former actor. The film earned rave reviews from critics. The worldwide collection for the film surpassed Rs. 450 crores, which made it a huge hit. The movie is also one of Indian cinema's biggest-grossing movies.  
  
Raghavan won several awards for [Andhadhun (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt8108198/?ls), including the National Film Award 2018 for Best Feature Film in Hindi, IIFA Award 2019 for Best Director, Best Story, and Best Screenplay, and Screen Award 2018 for Best Director and Best Film Writing (Story and Screenplay).

![Image 10: Ram Gopal Varma](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMTQ4NDQ0Mjc4OV5BMl5BanBnXkFtZTgwMjAxMTIzOTE@._V1_QL75_UY60_CR15,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0890060/?ref_=ls_i_8)  

 #### [8. Ram Gopal Varma](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0890060/?ref_=ls_t_8) 

    *   Director
    *   Producer
    *   Writer

[Rangeela (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0114234/?ref_=ls_knf_8)

Ram Gopal Varma was born in Hyderabad, the capital city of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. He initially was a video store owner before eventually becoming one of India's leading film directors. A film buff during his youth, Varma would watch both American and Indian cinema regularly. As a young man, he attended Siddhartha Engineering College in Vijayawada. Varma started his career in telugu cinema (the Hyderabad film industry), where he made a huge mark with his debut film Shiva, a violent and stylized actioner set in a college backdrop. At the age of 28, with little film training, Varma was able to convince Nagarjuna, a young Telugu star, to act in his debut picture. Nagarjuna was drawn by the narration of the script and intelligence displayed by the young Varma. Shiva was a landmark hit for the industry and was remade by Varma in the hindi language a year later.  
  
His next was the exciting adventure film, Kshana Kshanam, starring Venkatesh and Sridevi. Varma followed this up with such films as - Raatri, a homage to 'The Exorcist' starring Revati and Om Puri (which Varma would remake over a decade later in Hindi as Bhoot) and Antham, a stylized crime drama, with Nagarjuna and Urmila Matondkar (which Varma would also rework later as Satya) - but was not able to attain the commercial success of his first feature. His next release Gaayam, with Jagapathi Babu and Urmila Matondkar, was a violent crime drama set in Hyderabad. The screenplay was co-written by tamil film director Mani Ratnam, and the script based on 'The Godfather'. It became a success for Varma. He then decided to start his own production banner, Varma Corporation Limited, and produced successful telugu films such as Money (remade later as Love Ke Liye Kuchh Bhi Karega), Money Money (its sequel), Gulabi and Anaganaga Oka Roju.  
  
His first huge success in hindi cinema (the Mumbai film industry) was the commercial blockbuster Rangeela, a stylish romantic drama with Aamir Khan and Urmila Matondkar. A.R. Rahman, a tamil music composer, was introduced to hindi audiences by Varma with this film and won the award for best film music.  
  
Varma followed up with the ground breaking gangster saga Satya, a violent crime epic set in the Mumbai underworld. The film was gritty and realistic, reinventing the crime genre in Indian cinema. Varma had done extensive research for the film, and reworked certain elements of his earlier film Antham. Satya was widely considered Varma's first true masterwork. Made on a shoestring budget and with new faces, the film won awards for actor Manoj Bajpai and music composer Vishal Bharadwaj. Satya became a turning point in Varma's career, winning best picture of the year, and Varma would be forever associated with Mumbai noirs.  
  
Varma then, with fellow director Shekhar Kapur, created a joint film production company in 1998 called India Talkies. The first venture of the production house was the ambitious terrorist drama 'Dil Se', with Shahrukh Khan and Manisha Koirala. The film was a box office dud, and India Talkies would be short lived. Varma would return to focusing on his own production house Varma Corp.  
  
The hard hitting masterpiece 'Shool' followed shortly after, written and produced by Varma. The film depicted the life of an honest police officer in the violent and harsh rural setting of Bihar. The film was a commercial and critical success with both Manoj Bajpai and Sayaji Shinde winning awards for their performances. Varma lightened things up next with the romantic drama 'Mast'. The film was inspired by Varma's own college days, and featured Aftab Shivdasani in an award-winning turn as a film crazy college student.  
  
Varma decided afterwards to only direct films in the Mumbai film industry. He believed there was more talent in Mumbai than in southern film cities like Chennai and Hyderabad. Varma had always admired directors such as Shyam Benegal, Govind Nihlani, and Gulzar. He considers Kalyug, Ardh Satya, and Mere Apne among his favorite Indian films of all time. At a time when popular Indian Cinema featured either over the top action films or glamorous love stories, Varma's films were more rooted and realistic. Varma is known to frequently cut out song and dance sequences in his films, which are usually commonplace in Bollywood. His films almost always deal with the contemporary and urban, usually set in the city of Mumbai. He often uses Indian stage actors in his films rather than established bollywood stars. Mainly known for creating the 'Mumbai noir', Varma brought psychological depth and cinematic virtuosity to genre films.  
  
More recently, Varma returned with the organized crime masterpiece 'Company'. The film was again set in the Mumbai underworld, and was based on real life Underworld don Dawood Ibrahim and his criminal outfit D-Company. The film featured award-winning performances by Ajay Devgan, Vivek Oberoi and Manisha Koirala. The film also won awards for best editing by Chandan Arora and best story by Jaideep Sahni. The film was lauded by critics and audiences alike.  
  
His latest release Naach, which Varma called his best film yet, was a largely self reflective piece, about the relationship between an idealistic choreographer and an ambitious actor. The film had a weak commercial run but was liked by critics. In a recent interview with the Indian Express newspaper, the filmmaker criticized Indian audiences saying "I gave Ayn Rand to a Municipal School."  
  
He spends most of his time these days producing small budget films for his successful production house Varma Corp. Though not always credited, he is involved in all aspects of his productions, often believed to 'ghost direct' many of the films. He produces films at a fast speed that is unfamiliar to the Indian Film Industry. He has had many recent successes including - 'Ab Tak Chhappan', based on the experiences of famed Mumbai police Daya Naik, 'D', a prequel to his earlier hit Company based on the early years of Dawood Ibrahim during his days under Pathan underworld boss Karim Lala, 'Ek Hasina Thi', a female revenge thriller, and finally 'Road'. He has also produced lighter films such as 'Love Ke Liye Kuchh Bhi Karega' and 'Main Madhuri Dixit Banna Chahti Hoon'.

 #### [13. Deepa Mehta](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0576548/?ref_=ls_t_13)

[Fire (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0116308/?ref_=ls_knf_13)

Deepa Mehta is a transnational artist and a screenwriter, director, and producer whose work has been called "courageous", "provocative" and "breathtaking". Her visually lush and emotionally resonating films have played at every major international film festival; receiving numerous awards and accolades, and have been distributed around the world. Deepa was born in India and received a degree in philosophy from the University of New Delhi before immigrating to Canada. She began her career making documentaries in India.  
  
In 1991, Deepa's first feature film Sam & Me, which stars Om Puri, won a Special Jury Mention in the Camera D'Or section at the Cannes Film Festival. Between 1992-1994 she directed two episodes of The Young Indiana Jones, produced by George Lucas for ABC. In 1993, Deepa directed her second feature film Camilla, a Canada-UK co-pro starring Jessica Tandy, Bridget Fonda, Elias Koteas, Maury Chaykin, Graham Greene, and Hume Cronyn. Fire, which Deepa wrote and directed, is the first film in her Elemental Trilogy (Fire, Earth, Water). Fire opened Perspective Canada at the 1996 Toronto International Film Festival, where it was runner-up for the People's Choice Most Popular Film Award. It played at the New York Film Festival and won many awards worldwide, including the Audience Award for Best Canadian Film at the Vancouver International Festival, the Special Jury Prize at the Mannheim-Heidelberg International Film Festival and Silver Hugo Awards for Best Direction and Best Actress in Chicago.  
  
Earth, based on Bapsi Sidhwa's acclaimed novel about Partition, Cracking India, is the second film in the Elemental Trilogy. It premiered as a Special Presentation at the 1998 Toronto International Film Festival, and won the Prix Premiere du Public at the Festival du Film Asiatique de Deauville and the Critics' Award at the Verona Schermi d'Amore International Film Festival. Bollywood/Hollywood was a change of pace. Written and directed by Deepa, it is a lighthearted, affectionate comedy about two mismatched lovers. It opened Perspective Canada at the 2002 Toronto International Film Festival and was a tremendous crossover box office success. It remains one of the top 10 grossing English language Canadian movies. In 2003 Deepa co-wrote and directed the Canada-UK co-pro The Republic of Love, based on a Carol Shields novel.  
  
After a disrupted and hazardous production history Deepa's final film in the Elemental Trilogy Water opened the 2005 Toronto International Film Festival, and was the first Canadian film acquired by US distributor Fox Searchlight. Water is a powerful, hauntingly tragic story, set in Benares (Varanasi) about a child widow who at the age of eight is forced to enter a house of widows where she has to live for the rest of her life. The movie was to have been shot in India in 2000, but Hindu fundamentalists fomented riots, burnt sets, and issued death threats against the director and actors, forcing production to shut down and the filmmakers to leave the country. Water was successfully remounted in Sri Lanka and completed shooting in June 2004, and features many of India's most renowned actors.  
  
Water was an enormous success. It was nominated for an Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film at the 79th Annual Academy Awards, and has screened at festivals around the world, winning many awards, and remains an audience favourite. The Vancouver Film Critics Circle named Deepa Mehta the Best Canadian Director of 2006. This fall (2015) is the 10th anniversary of Water's launch.  
  
In 2006 Deepa made a documentary about domestic violence in Toronto's immigrant families called Let's Talk About It, which continues to be used in community outreach programs. She then thematically segued into the feature film Heaven On Earth, which explores arranged marriages and isolation. Starring Preity Zinta, the film had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2008. It was awarded a Silver Hugo for Best Actress at the Chicago International Film Festival, and received the Best Screenplay Award at the Dubai International Film Festival. It also won the Youth Jury Award at the Schermi d'Amore Film Festival in Verona and the Audience Award at the River to River Florence Indian Film Festival.  
  
In 2012, Deepa completed her epic cinematic adaptation of Salman Rushdie's famous novel about the history of India in the 20th century, Midnight's Children. A novel that won three Booker prizes. The movie, with 127 speaking parts, and covering five distinct time periods from 1917-1977, was a vast, ambitious undertaking and has screened all over the world, including the Telluride Film Festival, Toronto International Film Festival, Vancouver International Film Festival, and the BFI London Film Festival. Midnight's Children was chosen as the Best Feature Film of 2013 at the Directors Guild of Canada's Awards.  
  
Deepa's work as an artist, as a progressive voice about social issues, and her generous mentorship have often been recognized. She has received numerous honorary degrees and many awards and honours, among them: The Life of Distinction Award from the Canadian Centre of Diversity, The Excellence in the Arts Award from the Canadian Civil Liberties Association, and the Woman of Distinction, President's Award from the YMCA. She is a recipient of the Governor General's Lifetime Artistic Achievement Award for Film. Most recently, in 2013, Deepa was appointed as an officer to the Order of Canada, Canada's highest civilian honour, for her work as a "groundbreaking screenwriter, director, and producer." She is also a recipient of the province of Ontario's highest honour, the Order of Ontario.
